goal.text: Yeah is an Emacs Lisp agent harness: the harness runs in a dedicated Emacs process (the service placement); the model goes through gptel, every tool goes through the registry and the permission system, the session log stays append-only, and the editor reaches it through the bridge or an ACP/MCP client

claims.text: every file under lib/ byte-compiles without errors and without warnings
claims.falsifier: the byte-compilation of lib/ fails or reports a warning

claims.text: all ERT unit tests pass
claims.falsifier: an ERT unit test fails

claims.text: a session/cancel on the socket transport stops a running prompt
claims.falsifier: a cancel that arrives during a running prompt is read only after the prompt settles
claims.control: sed -i 's/(yeah-control-cancel (plist-get state :control) "cancelled by ACP client")/(progn)/' lib/yeah-acp.el

claims.text: the emacsclient bridge reads and edits the live buffers of a real Emacs server
claims.falsifier: the bridge is checked only against a stub, or a live read returns the wrong text

claims.text: two sessions in one Emacs run at once without cross-talk, and cancelling one leaves the other
claims.falsifier: an event of one run lands in the journal of the other

claims.text: the ACP and MCP servers answer over stdio with the real protocol
claims.falsifier: a stdio server does not answer or answers with the wrong protocol

claims.text: a 10 MiB token estimate does not block the event loop beyond a 100 ms timer
claims.falsifier: the estimate walks the text character by character and the timer fires seconds late

claims.text: the package entry declares the supported Emacs and gptel versions, and the bootstrap installs from lib/ with a pinned gptel
claims.falsifier: the package loses its version declaration or the bootstrap its lib layout

claims.text: a run starts from a snapshot of the registry; a tool one run registers is not advertised to another run or the shared registry
claims.falsifier: a tool one run registers appears in the shared registry or in another run
claims.control: sed -i 's|(puthash name spec (yeah-tools--active-registry))|(puthash name spec yeah-tools--registry)|' lib/yeah-tools.el

claims.text: a service Emacs starts, serves a prompt over the socket, writes the turn to its journal and stops
claims.falsifier: the service does not answer, or the journal has no turn

claims.text: the editor client connects to a service Emacs and drives a prompt over the socket, seeing the streamed updates
claims.falsifier: the client cannot connect, or the prompt is not answered, or no update arrives

claims.text: M-x yeah-service opens a buffer that drives a service Emacs: the question, the streamed answer and the stop reason are rendered
claims.falsifier: the buffer does not show the question, the answer or the stop reason

claims.text: an answer that only announces the next step, an answer that says nothing, or a result no tool backs, is nudged into the action; the run itself ends through the `finish' tool, and a result in words alone ends nothing.  The two claims of the completion path were in contradiction until wave 53: this one read the words of the model as the end of the run, and `finish-is-the-only-completion-path' read them as not an end at all.  The stricter reading won, because the architecture and the prelude of the harness both say that the run ends through the call of `finish'.
claims.falsifier: the run ends without acting, or a run that called the `finish' tool is nudged anyway, or a run that only reported its result in words ends as a completed job
claims.control: sed -i 's|(and (< (yeah-turn-nudge-spent turn) (yeah-turn-max-nudges turn))|(and nil (< (yeah-turn-nudge-spent turn) (yeah-turn-max-nudges turn))|' lib/yeah-turn.el

claims.text: an answer that arrives while the harness waits for a tool waits for the tools and ends the run instead of failing it
claims.falsifier: the run fails with no transition from awaiting-tool on stream-end
claims.control: sed -i 's|(setf (yeah-turn-pending-answer turn) answer)|(progn (yeah-turn--fail turn "late answer dropped") nil)|' lib/yeah-turn.el

claims.text: the standing permissions the person grants a service reach it: a tool the rules allow is allowed there, and a tool they do not name is asked of the client over the wire
claims.falsifier: the service denies a tool the person granted, or allows — without asking the client — a tool nobody granted

claims.text: a tool that registers another tool while it runs lands in the registry of the run, not in the shared one; the async-continuation path is documented, not silently wrong
claims.falsifier: a tool a run registers while it runs appears in the shared registry

claims.text: with supervision, the model ends the run by calling the finish tool; a text answer alone is not a completion.  A run that answers in words after its tools have run is nudged into the call of `finish', and a run that spends its budget without that call ends as a failed run that says it did not finish.
claims.falsifier: a run completes on a text answer alone when supervision is on, or a run that spent its budget ends without saying that it did not finish

claims.text: the descriptions of the built-in tools are unambiguous: read reads a file from disk by its path, buffer-read reads the content of a live Emacs buffer by its buffer name, every tool names the thing it works on, and no two tools share one description
claims.falsifier: read and buffer-read describe themselves the same way, or a tool description names another tool's subject, or two tools share one description
claims.control: sed -i 's|:description "Read the content of a live Emacs buffer.*"|:description "Read a file from disk by its path, from a 1-based line offset, up to a line limit. Use it for source code and for any file stored on disk."|' lib/yeah-emacs.el

claims.text: the task list of a run is a projection of its journal: the tools todo_add, todo_update and todo_list change the list through todo events of the session log, and a restart that reads the log again finds the same list
claims.falsifier: the task list is not the projection of the journal: the tools do not write the tasks into the log of the run, a restart that reads the log again does not restore the list, or the list survives the loss of its events

claims.text: the git tools show the status and the difference of a project, and write a commit only when the rules allow it
claims.falsifier: the status or the difference does not show the change, or a commit is written although no rule allows it
claims.control: sed -i 's|(user-error "the rules do not allow a commit|(message "the rules do not allow a commit|' lib/yeah-git.el

claims.text: a read of a file open in a buffer gives the model the modification tick it needs for a guarded edit
claims.falsifier: the model's view of a read has no tick

claims.text: the service asks the client before an effect the rules do not name
claims.falsifier: the tool runs although the client refused, or is denied although the client allowed

claims.text: the editor answers the service's permission request over the wire
claims.falsifier: the person's answer never reaches the service, or the question does not name the tool and its target
claims.control: sed -i 's|((and method id)|((and nil method id)|' lib/yeah-client.el

claims.text: the service socket lives where only this user can reach it
claims.falsifier: the socket sits bare in a world-writable directory, so any local user can drive the agent

claims.text: the client notices when the service is gone
claims.falsifier: the person types into a buffer nobody answers: the death of the service is not shown

claims.text: a clean service takes its model from the init file alone
claims.falsifier: the clean service has no model: the init file it loaded is ignored

claims.text: The session log on disk is append-only: every record written through yeah-session-append is appended to the JSONL file, so the file holds the header and every record in order with monotonic ids.
claims.falsifier: Reading the JSONL file after several appends shows any record missing, overwritten, or with non-monotonic ids — a writer that rewrites the file instead of appending loses the log while the in-memory list stays intact.

claims.text: The sessions of a project form a tree: an index lists every run under a root with its cost, and continuing a run from an earlier record keeps the abandoned path instead of deleting it.
claims.falsifier: The index misses a session or its cost, the reported/estimated tokens are lost, or branching at a record drops the abandoned records.

claims.text: A session exports to Org for the person: one heading per event, event fields as upper-case Org properties, and event text inside example blocks that Org cannot mistake for syntax, with the journal header excluded.
claims.falsifier: The export lacks the title or an event heading, loses a property, writes payload text outside an example block, exports the journal header, or the written file differs from the produced text.

claims.text: The journey of a person works end to end without a network: ask, watch the work in the view, steer a busy run, quit and restart with pending inputs intact, withdraw a steering, recover a pending input explicitly, and cancel a run — with each step journaled.
claims.falsifier: Any step of the journey breaks: the work does not journal the expected events, steering is not queued or survives a cancel, pending inputs vanish or auto-run after restart, withdrawal does not remove, recovery starts nothing, or a cancel does not stop the run and write the cancel record.

claims.text: The interface renders the run from the event stream and nothing else: the view built from the log records shows the transcript in order, each tool call with its final state and result, the approvals still waiting, and the counted cost.
claims.falsifier: The view diverges from the log: the transcript misses or misorders a message, a finished call is shown running or failed, answered approvals still show as pending, or the view reports a cost the log does not count.

claims.text: The ACP JSON-RPC dispatcher routes every method of the v1 surface (initialize, session/new, session/load, session/prompt, session/cancel), answers prompts asynchronously with a stop reason, and refuses unknown methods with -32601 and invalid requests with -32602.
claims.falsifier: The dispatcher fails to answer a v1 method, answers a prompt synchronously or without the end_turn stop reason, or answers an unknown method or an invalid request instead of refusing it with -32601/-32602.

claims.text: The ACP server completes the handshake, session creation, and an asynchronous prompt — including streamed session/update notifications and the end_turn stop reason — when driven by a third-party client (xenodium/acp.el) rather than by Yeah itself.
claims.falsifier: A third-party ACP client cannot initialize, open a session, or get a prompt answered with stopReason end_turn and session/update notifications from the Yeah server.

claims.text: A permission request is answered once, for the session, for the project, for the user or reject: once allows only this call, reject refuses only this call, the other three are written into the rules so they outlive the question — the rule of the answer session in the carrier of the path that asks, the rule of the answer project in the file of the project and the rule of the answer global in the file of the user — and every answer carries the scope its rule lives in; the legacy name `always' is read as the answer `session'; any other answer is refused, and an unattended run's policy allows exactly what the rules allow.
claims.falsifier: A reply of once/session/project/global/reject does not produce its documented decision, an answer is not written into the rules, an answer carries no scope or a scope that is not the scope of its rule, the legacy name `always' is not read as the answer `session', an invalid reply is accepted, or the policy answers contrary to the rules.

claims.text: The MCP tool registry in lib/yeah-emcp.el and the published schema schemas/emcp-v1.json name the same tools, with identical descriptions, inputs and outputs, and agree on which tools are published by default.
claims.falsifier: The registry and the schema drift apart: a different tool set, a differing description/input/output for any tool, or a different default-published set.
claims.control: sed -i 's/List live buffers, optionally filtered by a name prefix\./List every live buffer./' lib/yeah-emcp.el

claims.text: Every record written to the session log is one of the declared event types and carries exactly the fields its type declares; the writer refuses events of unknown type or with undeclared fields, and the todo event carries the tasks it changes and the operation that changed them.
claims.falsifier: The log holds an event of an undeclared type or with fields its type does not declare, the writer accepts such an event, or the todo event does not declare exactly :items and :operation.

claims.text: No Yeah kernel module installs or removes a global gptel hook; every gptel request is configured privately, per request.
claims.falsifier: A module under lib/ contains a call to add-hook or remove-hook on a gptel-* hook, creating a second, global integration path.

claims.text: The model is called in exactly one place, yeah-gptel-request in lib/yeah-gptel.el; no other kernel module calls gptel-request directly, and the turn reaches the model through that single bridge.
claims.falsifier: A lib module other than yeah-gptel.el contains a direct gptel-request call, or yeah-gptel-request does not exist, or the turn no longer goes through the bridge.

claims.text: yeah-gptel-request delivers the prompt unchanged, passes the caller's callback and the private system prompt to gptel, disables ambient gptel editor context, and returns the model's answer through the callback.
claims.falsifier: The adapter alters or drops the prompt, callback or system prompt on the way to gptel-request, or lets ambient gptel editor context leak into the request, or the answer never reaches the callback.

claims.text: The same task runs in all three placements — attached, service and batch — and each writes the same canonical projection of events to its session journal; a service run cannot see the editor's bridge tools without an operator decision.
claims.falsifier: Any placement fails to run the task to completion, the three journals disagree in their canonical event projections, the event sequence differs, or the bridge tool is registered without an operator decision.

claims.text: A sub-agent spawn whose child would reach the depth limit is refused with a user-error at spawn time, while a spawn within the limit is accepted.
claims.falsifier: A spawn at the boundary depth is accepted, or a spawn strictly within the limit is refused.
claims.control: sed -i 's/(>= (1+ depth) yeah-subagent--max-depth)/(> (1+ depth) yeah-subagent--max-depth)/' lib/yeah-subagent.el

claims.text: The experimental PTC evaluator refuses every form while disabled, runs ordinary registry tools through the permission system when explicitly enabled, and rejects direct and higher-order-function bypasses before anything is evaluated.
claims.falsifier: A form is evaluated while PTC is disabled, an allowed registry tool does not run when PTC is enabled, or a forbidden call is accepted and executes its side effect.
claims.control: sed -i "s/'(car cdr caar/'(delete-file car cdr caar/" lib/yeah-codes.el

claims.text: The pieces of the agent loop are actually wired together: yeah-loop-tick, yeah-perm-evaluate, yeah-tools-call and yeah-session-append are each called from at least one module outside the module that defines them.
claims.falsifier: Any of the four loop primitives has no caller outside its defining module — the modules exist but the loop does not run.

claims.text: a client that dies with a pending permission request does not hang the run: the service cancels it and writes the reason into the journal
claims.falsifier: the run still waits for an answer after its client disconnected, or the write ran although nobody allowed it

claims.text: The tool calls of one model answer run as a batch: shared calls overlap, an exclusive call runs alone, and the batch continuation fires only after every call has settled, with results in call order.
claims.falsifier: shared calls run one at a time, an exclusive call overlaps with another call, the batch settles before all calls have, or results come back out of order

claims.text: The runtime retries a failing command a bounded number of times, cuts a hanging command at its timeout and flags it as a timeout, detects doom loops of identical mutating calls while allowing repeated read-only inspection, and never holds the main loop.
claims.falsifier: a failing command is not retried, a hanging command is not cut or not marked as a timeout, repeated mutation is not seen as a loop, or repeated read-only inspection is flagged as one

claims.text: A turn asks the model, runs the permitted tool calls through the permission system and the registry, appends what happened to the session log, and refuses a denied call without running it, logging the refusal.
claims.falsifier: a permitted call does not run or is not logged in order, or a denied call runs anyway or is not logged as a refusal

claims.text: Malformed arguments, handler exceptions, duplicate async callbacks and nil results become bounded string failures handed to the model once — the turn never wedges, never logs a failure as a success, and never settles one call twice.
claims.falsifier: a tool failure wedges the turn or escapes as an error, a failed call is logged as a success, a duplicate async callback settles the call twice, or a nil result reaches the model instead of an explicit error string

claims.text: When the context overflows, the turn enters the compacting state without blocking, waits for the asynchronously arriving summary, commits it as a compaction record before the continued answer, and keeps the source tool events.
claims.falsifier: the turn blocks waiting for the summary, completes without the committed compaction record, orders the compaction after the continued answer, or loses the source tool events

claims.text: The built-in coding tools work end to end on a real temporary project: read, glob and grep find content, a fresh modification tick guards a real buffer edit, elisp-check validates the result, async bash settles through its continuation, introspection answers, and every built-in tool is registered.
claims.falsifier: discovery misses the file, a tick-fresh edit is rejected or does not change the buffer, the edited Elisp is unreadable, async bash never settles or returns wrong output, introspection fails, or a built-in tool is missing from the registry
claims.control: sed -i 's|(if (and tick (/= tick current-tick))|(if tick|' lib/yeah-edit.el

claims.text: Context usage is counted, overflow is detected, the summary is written by the model and not by a placeholder, compaction appends its record while keeping the summarised sources on disk, and pruning marks old outputs without deleting records.
claims.falsifier: usage or overflow is not seen, the summary does not come from the model, compaction leaves no record or drops sources, or pruning deletes records instead of marking them

claims.text: Compaction is a projection, not a deletion: the on-disk log after a compaction holds exactly the source records plus one appended compaction record, with every source byte-for-byte untouched.
claims.falsifier: the log is shorter or longer than sources-plus-one after a compaction, the source records changed, or the trailing record is not the compaction

claims.text: The person-facing projection correlates parallel same-name tool calls, approvals and terminal results by stable tool-call id, and never guesses when an id is ambiguous.
claims.falsifier: A parallel same-name tool call, its approval or its result is attached to another call, or an ambiguous legacy record is presented as a confident correlation.

claims.text: The shared journal preserves the person's reading position while it updates, and every semantic label keeps readable text when optional icons are unavailable.
claims.falsifier: An update moves a reader away from the passage being read, erases a block, or replaces a readable label with an icon-only or empty string.
claims.control: sed -i 's/(unless following/(when following/' lib/yeah-journal.el && sed -i 's/(yeah-faces--label-text label (plist-get spec :label))/(format "" (plist-get spec :label))/' lib/yeah-faces.el

claims.text: Attached and service placements show the same question, answer and terminal state in the same shared read-only journal; the service path is driven through a real Emacs process and a real client connection.
claims.falsifier: Either placement renders a different or duplicated transcript, exposes an editable transcript, loses the answer or stop reason, or the service path stops being a real process and client connection.

claims.text: A narration nudge names the exact next call: the unused path tool, the file the model named, and on a repeat it requires the next answer to contain the tool call, not another plan.
claims.falsifier: the nudge lists tools without naming the call to make, names no path argument or file, or a repeated nudge does not require an action
claims.control: sed -i 's/Make this call now/Continue when ready/g' lib/yeah-turn.el

claims.text: The bridge does not lose the answer of the attached Emacs: a process that exits before its last chunk reaches the filter still delivers the answer.
claims.falsifier: the bridge answers with an empty output although the attached Emacs printed the answer

claims.text: the check of the bridge gives the same verdict on ten consecutive runs of the control, and the control bites on each of them
claims.falsifier: the check of the bridge gives different verdicts on consecutive runs of the control, or the control does not bite on each of them

claims.text: A supervised run whose nudge budget is spent without the model finishing writes the unfinished event: a run that ends without the effect must not look done.
claims.falsifier: the run ends as if the work were done although the model never finished

claims.text: A supervised run that ended without the effect is visible where the person looks: the view says unfinished, the journal shows the reason, and the run is never shown as finished.
claims.falsifier: the run that ended without the effect looks finished, or the reason is not shown

claims.text: The question of the permission is asked in one place: the shared approval view, which names the action, the resource it acts on, the arguments it would run with and the diff of the change, and which offers the four scopes of an answer — once, session, project and global — and the refusal, each named by what it allows; the attached and the service path both answer there.
claims.falsifier: A path asks the permission somewhere else, or the view does not name what the person is asked about, or the view does not offer the scopes it offers.

claims.text: the Yeah composer turns its buffer into one prompt: sending passes the trimmed text and the explicit file/buffer context to the target, and the prompt is remembered in a bounded newest-first history
claims.falsifier: the composer sends text other than the buffer's text, drops the explicit context, or the history is not newest-first or not bounded
claims.control: sed -i 's/(funcall target text context)/(funcall target text nil)/' lib/yeah-compose.el

claims.text: a Yeah edit or write is previewed as a unified diff of the proposed change, and previewing changes neither the file on disk nor the modification tick or the undo list of a visited buffer
claims.falsifier: the preview omits the proposed change, or previewing alters the file, the modification tick of a visited buffer or its undo list
claims.control: sed -i 's/(yeah-diff--unified current changed)/(yeah-diff--unified current current)/' lib/yeah-diff.el

claims.text: Yeah's doctor reports more than five local checks in a readable buffer and prints no API key and no bearer token
claims.falsifier: the report has fewer than six checks, the rendered buffer does not name the doctor, or it prints an api key or a bearer token
claims.control: sed -i 's/No API keys or secrets are printed\./api_key: leaked/' lib/yeah-doctor-ui.el

claims.text: the Yeah session list shows the sessions of one project and hands the id of the selected session to its opener, and it never deletes or rewrites a session
claims.falsifier: the list hides a session of the project, or the id of the selected session is not passed to the opener, or the list deletes or rewrites a session
claims.control: sed -i 's/(funcall yeah-session-list--open id)/(funcall yeah-session-list--open nil)/' lib/yeah-session-list.el

claims.text: the optional Markdown adapter fontifies a copy of the region and copies only face properties into the target buffer, leaving its text, major mode, narrowing, read-only state and modification tick untouched; without the package it is a plain-text no-op
claims.falsifier: the adapter changes the text, the major mode, the narrowing or the read-only state of the target buffer, copies a property other than a face, or marks the buffer modified; without markdown-mode it still changes the region
claims.control: sed -i "s/(dolist (property '(face font-lock-face))/(dolist (property '(face font-lock-face invisible display))/" lib/yeah-markdown.el

claims.text: A read that changes nothing is not asked about: the permission layer answers it and says why, in the profile of a run and over the wire alike.
claims.falsifier: a read is asked about although nothing changes, or the decision does not say why nobody was asked

claims.text: An answer of always is remembered: the rule of the decision reaches the rules of the run or the session, so the same question is not asked again.
claims.falsifier: the decision is allowed but forgotten, so the person is asked the same question twice

claims.text: The pending queue of a session is a projection of the journal: every input that is queued, starts a run, is recovered or is withdrawn is written into the session log with its id, and the pending list of the editor agrees with the queue of the controller.
claims.falsifier: the journal carries no queue event, or the wrong input id, or a withdrawn input stays in the pending list of the editor
claims.control: sed -i 's/(yeah-control--write-withdrawn control input "withdrawn by the person")/(ignore input)/' lib/yeah-control.el

claims.text: A permission request is written into the journal before the question is asked, and an answer that comes later settles the question exactly once.
claims.falsifier: the request is not in the log when the answerer is asked, or a second answer changes the decision, or a question that is not answered in time is not refused with a reason

claims.text: The ACP wire carries the control of a session: a client steers a running turn, withdraws a pending input, recovers one, opens the session again with its journal replayed, and the pending queue of the session reaches the client that asked for the queue events as session/update notifications.
claims.falsifier: the steer, the withdraw or the recover is not answered, the replay carries no earlier record, or the pending queue of the session does not reach the client that asked for the queue events as a session/update

claims.text: The self-check proves every task of the task set has a prompt and an executable check that fails on an untouched workspace, and the runner records a harness that could not run as skipped or not-available, never as a pass.
claims.falsifier: a check of the task set passes on an untouched workspace, or a harness that could not run is recorded as a pass

claims.text: The command `M-x yeah' opens the service placement, and falls back to the attached placement when the service cannot start.
claims.falsifier: the entry point opens the attached placement while the service is available, or the service fails and the attached path does not open

claims.text: The editor sends the control requests of a service session — steer, withdraw and recover — over the wire, and the queue notifications that arrive populate its pending-input view.
claims.falsifier: a control request is absent or carries the wrong parameters, or a queued event that arrives over the wire is absent from the pending-input view

claims.text: The editor finds a service through a Unix-domain socket on Unix and through a numeric port file on a loopback TCP port when IPv4 is selected.
claims.falsifier: the IPv4 service publishes no numeric port file, the client cannot connect through it, or the file remains after the service stops

claims.text: An answer of the model that says nothing is not a result: with supervision the run nudges the model into the action, and without supervision the run fails instead of ending as a finished job.
claims.falsifier: a run that received an empty answer ends as a finished job without a nudge and without saying that it did not finish

claims.text: A nudge that follows an empty answer carries the state of the work — the tools the run already called and the results they returned — and does not name an unused tool as the next call, so that the model continues instead of starting the work over.
claims.falsifier: the nudge that follows an empty answer names a tool as the next call and does not say what the run has already done

claims.text: An edit of a file that no buffer visits is not refused because of a tick the model could not have read: only a buffer that visits the file hands out a tick, so a tick for a file nobody had open is a guess, and the guard keeps the ticks that a read handed out.
claims.falsifier: the edit of a file that no buffer visits is refused as stale although the file did not change, or the guard stops refusing a stale tick of a file that a buffer visits
claims.control: sed -i 's|(if existing expected-tick nil)|(if existing expected-tick expected-tick)|' lib/yeah-edit.el

claims.text: A run that the provider or the transport to it stopped is recorded as blocked and not as a failure of the agent: a provider that fails is not an agent that fails, and the measurement of nothing is not a failure.
claims.falsifier: the runner records a run that the provider stopped as a failure of the agent or as a pass

claims.text: A decision that arrives while the tools of the previous decision are still running waits for them: the run does not break, the decision is not lost, and the model sees the results of every batch together.
claims.falsifier: a decision that arrives while the tools run ends the run in failure, or the decision is dropped and never runs

claims.text: A tool call that is already running is not run again: the model that says the same thing twice runs the tool once, because a tool that runs twice repeats its side effect.
claims.falsifier: a tool call that is running runs a second time while it runs

claims.text: A read hands the model a version token of the file it read, and an edit that presents that token is refused when the file changed after the read: an edit never lands on a file the model did not read.
claims.falsifier: the edit of a file that changed after the read is applied anyway, or the read hands out no version to guard the edit with

claims.text: A tool call that is dropped as a repeat is written into the journal: a reader of the log tells a repeated decision from a decision that never came.
claims.falsifier: the journal holds no record of the dropped decision, or the reader cannot tell the drop from a decision that never came
claims.control: sed -i 's|(yeah-turn--note-drop turn call)|(ignore "the drop is not written")|' lib/yeah-turn.el

claims.text: The version token that a read hands out is short enough for a model to copy it back unchanged: the token of the pilot of 2026-11-15 was 64 characters of hex, and the model presented 58 of them.
claims.falsifier: the token of a read is longer than a model can copy back, or it does not change when the text changes

claims.text: An edit that presents a version token which is not the version of the file now is refused, and the refusal names the token and reports the current one: a token that was copied wrong does not mean that the file changed, and the retry with the reported token lands.
claims.falsifier: the refusal does not report the current token of the file, or it tells the model that the file changed when it did not
claims.control: sed -i 's|The file may be unchanged and the token may have been copied wrong|The file changed since the read|' lib/yeah-edit.el

claims.text: An edit of a file that Emacs holds unsaved changes of is refused, with a version or without one: a read of the file shows the disk and cannot show the changes of the person, so the edit would overwrite them with text the model never read.
claims.falsifier: the edit of a file that Emacs holds unsaved changes of is applied anyway, or the refusal depends on the model presenting a version

claims.text: A write that replaces a file presents the version of the read that it follows and is refused when the file changed since that read: a write never lands on a file the model did not read.

claims.text: Every cell of the table of the machine is a move the runtime takes: the machine makes the move of every cell, the runtime takes the label of the cell in a live place of the code — a place the runtime runs, and not one that only a name, a test or a script reaches, and not one that stands in no definition of the kernel — and the place names the state the cell leads from — or the place names no state at all, and the cell rests on the machine alone, and the check names such places and such labels by their file and their line; the runtime takes no move the machine does not have, and a place whose label the check cannot read is a defect of its own that the check names by its file and its line; a fan of a label is not narrowed by the runtime wherever the runtime states the whole coverage of that fan — the one fan whose coverage the runtime does not state, `interrupt`, is named by the check as such — every fan ends the run in one state, and every state of the machine is reachable from the first one through the cells of the table; and the walk of the code reads a name as a name and not as a call — a name in a quoted list, a name in a list of names (the parameters of a `lambda`, the names of the bindings of a `let`, the variable of the spec of a `dolist`, the pattern of a `pcase`, the types of the handlers of a `condition-case`, the type and the slots of a `cl-defstruct`, the name of a derived mode) calls nothing, and a tick that stands in data is no place of the runtime; and the walk knows the position of every form it meets — the special forms of Emacs are read out of Emacs itself, the macros of the kernel out of the files of the kernel, and the forms the walk meets out of the walk itself — and a form that the table of the positions does not know is a defect of the check, named by its file and its line; and the body of a local function that the runtime never calls is not code the runtime runs, and a name in a quoted form is data and not a call.
claims.falsifier: a cell of the table of the machine is not a move the machine makes, or a label of the table has no live place in the runtime where a run takes that move, or a live place takes the move of a cell from a state the cell does not lead from, or the runtime takes a move the machine does not have, or the runtime takes a move whose label the check cannot read, or a place of the runtime that stands in no definition of the kernel witnesses a cell, or a name that stands in a position where a name stands is read as a call, or a tick that stands in data is read as a place of the runtime, or a form that the walk meets is not in the table of the positions, or the body of a local function that the runtime never calls is read as a place of the runtime, or a name in a quoted form is read as a call, or the runtime narrows a fan of the table whose coverage the runtime states in full, or a fan of the table does not end in one state, or a state of the machine is not reachable from the first one through the cells of the table, or the check measured the table differently than it measured it before, or the control of the claim does not make the check fail by its own assertion
claims.control: sed -i "s|(compacting       error         . failed)|(compacting       interrupt     . interrupted)|" lib/yeah-loop.el && sed -i "s|(when (eq (yeah-turn-state turn) 'idle)|(when (eq (yeah-turn-state turn) 'deciding)|" lib/yeah-turn.el

claims.text: Every kind a tool declares is in the vocabulary of the protocol, and a kind outside it never passes silently: the tool that declares it is refused by name, and the kind of a call that carries it is never quietly replaced by `other'.

claims.text: The pipeline of the diagrams renders every diagram in both themes: `scripts/dev diagrams` finds PlantUML by itself — every step of the chain of the search works alone (the environment, PATH, the profile of the user, the store of nix), and the chain of the search lives in one place in `scripts/`: `scripts/dev` reads it from `scripts/lib/tools.sh`, calls it, and writes no step of the search of a tool by itself; no other script of `scripts/` defines the chain or carries a copy of its body, and a copy of the body that is rewritten in other words is not seen — the searches of the checks themselves are their own, by design — and the chain is proved by the behaviour of the pipeline and not by its wording: in a copy of the tree whose chain hands out a decoy instrument the pipeline draws the pictures of the decoy, so a pipeline that takes the instrument from anywhere but the chain of the search is seen — answers with the code 3 when the tool is not there, answers with the code 1 when PlantUML fails or writes no picture, and writes two pictures for every diagram of the tree into `site/assets/diagrams/` — the light one and the dark one — each picture drawn from the whole of its own source, with the skin of the site, whose colours are the tokens of the site.  The decoy is measured in the environment of a normal run, where every step of the chain of the search resolves — the variable of the environment, the command on the PATH, the binary of the profile of the user and the glob of the store of nix — and the boundary of the probe is named: the decoy sees a copy that resolves the instrument in the environment of the decoy, and it does not see a copy that resolves it in a place that the environment of the decoy does not provide.
claims.falsifier: a step of the chain of the search does not work alone, or the chain of the search is copied in a second place, or the pipeline does not read the chain from the place where it lives, or the pipeline writes a step of the search of a tool by itself, or the pipeline takes the instrument from anywhere but the chain of the search, or the pipeline renders one theme only, or a diagram of the tree is not drawn, or a picture is not drawn from its own source, or a picture is drawn from a part of its source, or the pipeline answers with the code 0 when the tool is not there, or the pipeline answers with the code 0 when PlantUML fails or writes no picture, or the skins of the themes do not carry the colours of the site, or the decoy is measured in an environment in which a copy of the chain cannot resolve the instrument and a pipeline that takes the instrument from that copy is not seen, or the control of the claim does not make the check fail by its own assertion
claims.control: sed -i 's|for theme in light dark; do|for theme in light; do|' scripts/dev

claims.text: The picture of the layers of the core names the code that implements it, and every name it gives points at what is there: every reference of the form `file:line' of `site/diagrams/core-layers.puml' names a file of this repository, a line of that file and a line that carries a definition -- an empty line names no code, a line that holds nothing but a comment names no code either, and a line that holds code and no definition names no definition -- a reference to a path that leaves the repository names nothing of this repository, every module of `lib/' is named by the picture or listed in the note of the modules the picture does not name with the reason why it is not there, the note names no module that is not there, names no module without a reason and names no module that the picture names as well, every block of the picture names at least one file, and the four layers of the picture -- the drivers, the core, the journal and the projections -- are there.

claims.text: A tool declares whether it changes the world: the field is `:risk', its values come from the vocabulary of the kernel (`read', `write', `execute' or `destroy'), and the permission rule asks by that declaration and not by the name of a tool in a list. claims.text: A process that is dead is dead everywhere: the rule of the life of a process lives in the kernel, in one place (`lib/yeah-proc.el'), and it answers by the state of the process -- `S' and `R' live, `Z' is a zombie and a zombie is dead, every other letter does not run, and the state `nil' is a process that is not there at all. The kernel asks the rule in both of its places (`lib/yeah-life.el'), so the socket of a zombie owner is swept away and a zombie owner is not adopted as if it lived, and the checks of `tests/checks/' read the process through the one reader and not by a path of their own -- the check that proves the claim of the wave 100 is the one exception, and it reads the stat file of its own process to compare the answer of the reader with the truth --.

claims.text: A tool declares the limits it has: the field `:timeout` is the upper bound of the work one call of the tool may start, in seconds, and the field `:output-limit` is the upper bound of the output one call of the tool may hand to the model, in characters.
